papers.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
papers.abstract: Commercial detectors of AI-generated audio are usually promoted with results on internal test sets that buyers cannot inspect. Independent benchmarks with private labels give a more reliable comparison. We report the results of Neural Defend's ARCAS foundation models on the Podonos audio deepfake detection benchmark, an independent leaderboard that scores commercial detection APIs and open-source detectors on one held-out set of real speech and speech from current text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, delivered in six file formats, against labels that only Podonos holds. In the release of 29 October 2026, which covers 28 systems from 16 commercial vendors and the leading open models, ARCAS 290M and the smaller ARCAS 90M share first place, ahead of every other commercial system, including Resemble AI, Hiya, Pindrop, Hive, and Reality Defender. Both models make fewer errors than any other system by a statistically clear margin, keep false positives and false negatives in balance at their default threshold, process every submitted file without rejection, and sit on the accuracy--latency frontier of the leaderboard. As for every commercial system added since Podonos retired its API runner, the ARCAS predictions were submitted by Neural Defend and scored by Podonos against its private labels. We describe the benchmark's construction and protocol in full, reproduce the complete leaderboard and its history across five releases, and analyse error balance, statistical separation, speed, and the gap between commercial and open-source detectors. The results agree with the companion evaluation of ARCAS 290M on the complete test sets of ten public benchmarks and establish ARCAS as the most accurate AI-generated audio detector evaluated on this independent benchmark.
reasons: Evaluation, Alignment, Safety & Copyright: audio deepfake

papers.title: Windchime: an Audiovisual Installation with Audio-Language Model implementations
papers.abstract: Windchime is an audiovisual installation in which spoken language retrieves music and interactive animations from an artist authored corpus. A local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model transcribes each prompt while an audio-language model (ALM) embeds it and retrieval over 406 audio stems returns a soundscape with live coded Strudel fragments that layer into audio output. Simultaneously each spoken input results in retrieval of interactive Three.js animation scenes each containing unique tactile control via monome grid and arc hardware. Windchime distributes agency in three distinct directions; across the artist who authored the possible outputs, the ALM that influences what areas of the corpus can be retrieved, and the visitor whose spoken inputs result in multimodal embodied interaction.
papers.venue: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track (artwork). 4 pages (3 pages plus references), 2 figures. Video: https://youtu.be/j3XyW2ynH5Y OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=KKLTKVVHkM NeurIPS: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/loc/sydney/160685

papers.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
papers.abstract: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. We introduce Speech Language Pathologist Bench (SLP-Bench), a benchmark grading each acoustic claim in the chain of thought against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. It covers five clinician-rated datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions, and assesses claims for factuality, stability under resampling, and consistency across reworded and different questions. Across ten open-weight reasoning ALMs evaluated zero-shot, claim balanced accuracy ranges from 0.52 to 0.58, claims change under resampling and rewording, and the most consistent models are not the most factual. Fine-tuning a 7B ALM with GRPO on a reward for claims that agree with clinicians raises its claim balanced accuracy from 0.54 to 0.60 and its mean kappa from 0.39 to 0.61, while preserving answer accuracy on per-dimension questions. SLP-Bench is available upon request, subject to approval by the providers of each dataset.
papers.venue: 5 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, submitted to ICASSP 2027 workshop "Explainability, Robustness, and Controllability of Language Modeling for Speech and Audio"

papers.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
papers.abstract: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the Podonos leaderboard and has the lowest equal error rate among commercial detectors on ASVspoof5. It separates real from AI-generated speech almost perfectly on ASVspoof5, SpeechFake, and ShiftySpeech, and detects nearly all AI-generated speech in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, and Telugu. On every benchmark with a published zero-shot comparison, including in-the-wild audio, partial fakes, and the conditions hardest for the field, it surpasses the strongest reported detector by a wide margin. These results establish ARCAS 290M as a general-purpose foundation for AI-generated audio detection in fraud prevention, platform safety, and media verification.
reasons: Speech Generation, Recognition & Dialogue: text-to-speech, voice cloning

papers.title: Granary-v2: Scalable Multilingual Speech Data Curation for Predictable and Controllable Model Outputs
papers.abstract: Speech-language models that follow instructions need training data that connects the same recording to different output forms and tasks. We present Granary-v2, a multilingual speech dataset and reusable curation system that provides a data foundation for these models. Granary-v2 extends Granary-v1 with aligned transcript variants and instruction-target pairs for multi-task speech-language training. Language coverage increases from 25 to 48 languages. Built with NeMo Curator, the system combines language-dependent ASR labeling, transcript improvement, and text label generation. It produces aligned targets for speech-faithful transcription, written forms with and without disfluencies, and code-switched transcription. Additional targets include transcript-derived captions and question-answer pairs, with context and translations for selected records. The full processed collection contains approximately 843,600 unique audio hours, with translations covering about 142,800 hours into English and about 55k hours of English audio into 31 target languages. We evaluate label-quality filtering with two English Transformer-TDT models under the same training-step budget. Filtering reduces the unweighted mean word error rate across nine benchmarks from 4.91% to 4.67%, with improvements on six benchmarks. We also report curation throughput and downstream ASR and speech translation results from Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, which uses Granary-v2 as part of its training data. We release the Granary-v2 pipeline, built with NeMo Curator, and model training recipes as open source. We release a public subset of the generated labels and instruction-target pairs through Hugging Face.
papers.venue: The first three authors contributed equally. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Granary-v2

papers.title: Preserving Prosody in Speaker Anonymization
papers.abstract: Effective prosody modeling is essential in natural speech generation applications, but complications arise in speaker anonymization, since speaker attributes are present in acoustic correlates of prosody. Our work aims to improve previous reported tradeoffs between effective speaker obfuscation and preservation of prosodic content. To this end, we integrate an existing pretrained privacy-preserving prosody encoder into a speech synthesis model, enabling prosody-preserving speaker anonymization. By conditioning speech generation on prosody features, we find that human subjects more reliably perceive intended prosodic meaning, while anonymization performance is competitive with previous work.
reasons: Speech Generation, Recognition & Dialogue: speech generation, speech synthesis

papers.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
papers.abstract: Spoken dialogue synthesis aims to generate multi-turn conversational speech from dialogue scripts while maintaining speaker consistency and contextual appropriateness. However, existing models largely lack fine-grained controllability, which is critical for capturing the dynamic, context-dependent style shifts in natural conversations. While prompt-based TTS has enabled such control for single-speaker speech, existing datasets heavily rely on predefined tags, which fundamentally limits their capacity to capture open-ended styles. To address this gap, we propose a scalable pipeline for extracting conversational speech from multi-narrator audiobooks, featuring an improved two-stage alignment algorithm to preserve dialogue continuity, paired with LLM-based extraction of style descriptions directly from narrative text. We release PromptDialog, a large-scale multi-speaker conversational speech dataset comprising 8,383 hours of Chinese speech and 120 hours of English speech, with open-ended style descriptions for 79% of utterances. We further introduce PromptTTSD, a spoken dialogue synthesis model built via a prompt-aware fine-tuning strategy that integrates style prompts into text-speech interleaved sequences. PromptTTSD is an open-source spoken dialogue synthesis model that supports both zero-shot voice cloning and natural language style control. Experiments demonstrate that PromptTTSD not only maintains strong fundamental synthesis capabilities but also achieves competitive open-ended style control compared with proprietary models, and substantially improves contextual appropriateness in multi-turn dialogues.
papers.venue: 16 pages, 5 figures, 12 tables. Corresponding authors: Zhi Zeng, Shuwu Zhang, and Shuo Chen
reasons: Speech Generation, Recognition & Dialogue: voice cloning

papers.title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS
papers.abstract: Latent text-to-speech (TTS) systems generate codec latents decoded by a frozen decoder, but good reconstruction does not ensure geometry suitable for Flow generation from isotropic Gaussian noise. We present Embedded Acoustic Flow TTS (EAF-TTS), an acoustic-latent adaptation of ELF with phone- and duration-conditioned generation, shared-network terminal correction, and frozen WaveVAE decoding. EAF-TTS supports a fixed ZCA interface estimated from training data and adding no learned parameters. The codec, conditioning modules, Flow backbone, and 20-call inference are shared. The intervention is the full ZCA coordinate protocol---training and sampling coordinates, induced loss metric, and terminal perturbation---not an inference-only transform. In single-speaker LJSpeech, the 64-D training-latent covariance has condition number 1355.44. On text-disjoint Val399 strict-GT with fixed E100 raw checkpoints across three matched seeds, ZCA improves UTMOS22 Strong---an automatic naturalness proxy, not human MOS---by $+0.405\pm0.027$ over Scalar normalization (mean $\pm$ seed SD of per-seed paired differences). Absolute scores remain below codec-reference levels. Without retraining, ZCA-5 retains $+0.375\pm0.027$ UTMOS over Scalar-20 while reducing generation-path RTF by $3.34\times$. This three-seed analysis shows no statistically detectable WER or exact-match degradation, but does not establish equivalence. ZCA-3 gives $5.03\times$ with a $+0.165$ UTMOS advantage. At matched reduced call counts, ZCA's advantage shrinks, indicating full-step headroom rather than better low-step integration. A secondary text-only selected-checkpoint result is directionally consistent but confounded by checkpoint type. We claim only proxy-naturalness and measured quality--latency effects within this protocol; human listening, blind text, and broader validation remain necessary.

papers.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems perform strongly on native-English benchmarks, yet their accuracy degrades sharply when the input speech comes from under represented non-native accents. Nepali-accented English is particularly under-served: existing resources either focus on native Nepali speech, cover broader multi-accent settings without dedicated Nepali evaluation, or provide only limited Nepali-accent coverage. This paper presents a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset designed to support robust ASR benchmarking under accent mismatch. The corpus was collected through a web-based platform that did not collect directly identifying metadata and contains recordings from 57 speakers. Each session follows a fixed 22-prompt protocol consisting of 11 phonetic prompts, 10 domain prompts, and 1 spontaneous prompt, providing complementary coverage of pronunciation, topical vocabulary, and natural speaking style. In addition to transcribed speech, the dataset includes participant metadata for coarse exploratory subgroup analysis and speaker-level manual recording-quality labels. Manual quality assessment shows that 50.9% of sessions are clean and 42.1% contain only mild noise. As a descriptive reference, open-source ASR baselines are substantially worse on this corpus than the corresponding LibriSpeech test-clean values reported in official model cards, reaching 38.15-55.00% WER on the collected set versus reported 2-4% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean. These baseline results position the corpus as a practical held-out resource for evaluating accent robustness and out-of-distribution generalization on Nepali-accented English.
reasons: Speech Generation, Recognition & Dialogue: automatic speech recognition

Sori-10B-Speech

Seonuk Kim  ·  Semin Kim  ·  Beom Jun Woo  ·  🇰🇷
{sukim, smkim21, bjwoo}@hi.snu.ac.kr

*Sori* (소리) is Korean for *sound*. Sori-10B-Speech is a speech LLM that hears how things are said (tone, hesitation, emotion, who is speaking and in what state) and uses those cues when it reasons. ## Usage ```python # pip install "transformers>=5.23" soundfile import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor repo = "snkii/Sori-10B-Speech" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto") audio, sr = sf.read("speech.wav", dtype="float32") # 16 kHz mono messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio"}, {"type": "text", "text": "How does the speaker sound, and why?"}, ]}] prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) inputs = processor(text=prompt, audio=audio, sampling_rate=sr, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) print(processor.decode(output[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)) ``` Several clips and questions in one batch: ```python files = ["a.wav", "b.wav", "c.wav"] questions = ["How does the speaker sound, and why?", "What is the speaker's mood?", "Is the speaker hesitant?"] audios = [sf.read(f, dtype="float32")[0] for f in files] # 16 kHz mono prompts = [processor.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio"}, {"type": "text", "text": q}, ]}], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) for q in questions] inputs = processor(text=prompts, audio=audios, sampling_rate=16000, padding=True, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) for answer in processor.batch_decode(output[:, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True): print(answer) ``` ## License Sori-10B-Speech is released under **[CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/)**: use it and build on it for non-commercial purposes, with attribution, and share what you derive from it under the same terms. Commercial use is not licensed because part of the training data is licensed for non-commercial use. Third-party components keep their own licenses, which will be listed with the weights. ## Citation ```bibtex @software{kim_sori_10b_speech_2026, author = {Kim, Seonuk and Kim, Semin and Woo, Beom Jun}, title = {{Sori-10B-Speech}}, year = {2026}, institution = {Human Interface Laboratory, Seoul National University}, url = {https://huggingface.co/snkii/Sori-10B-Speech} } ```

It listens while you talk, decides from your voice when you have finished, writes a reply with sound tags (`[laughter]` `[cough]` `[sigh]` `[breath]` `…`) and speaks while it writes; a lighter, faster speech model speaks the tagged reply (one forward pass per 80 ms frame). Speech only: the 4B brain has no vision. For the strongest answers, use the 32B builds ([Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag) · [Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) · [E2E](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E)) or the [hosted API](https://api.adventists.ai/console/). ## Benchmarks | | 4B | 32B (published) | |---|---|---| | VoiceBench overall | 62.4 | 82.8 | | Big Bench Audio (spoken answer, transcribed) | 44.3% | 81.8% | | Full-Duplex-Bench v1.0, Flash build (avg of 2 pause tasks, turn-taking, interruption) | 87.7 | 94.0 | | Sound-tag rate on held-out conversations (reference: 0.36) | 0.36 | — | **What 4B is for.** The 4B brain keeps the conversation skills of the family: listening while you talk, deciding when you have finished, back-channels, barge-in and sound tags (Full-Duplex-Bench close to the 32B builds, and the same tag rate as the reference data). Use it for local demos, companions and characters, and research on turn-taking; use the 32B builds or the hosted API when answers must be right. Among open full-duplex models, its VoiceBench score is above Freeze-Omni (55.2) and Moshi (29.5) and below MiniCPM-o (71.2). VoiceBench: official evaluators, gpt-4o-mini judge, AlpacaEval on the standard 199-question subset, overall = mean of 9 tasks. Big Bench Audio: 1,000 questions, GPT-4.1 judges the transcript of the spoken answer. [All builds](https://huggingface.co/collections/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime-6afb357253a3a8905ad758b0) **Version 1.2.0** (2026-11-13) · [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · [▶ v1.1 demo video](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime#zero-shot-voice-cloning-new-in-v11) Code and one-command deployment: [github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/tree/main/tag](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/tree/main/tag) · Built on [DuplexJev](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev) · Voice: [tag-tts](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/tag-tts) **The Tag build of Sophon-Realtime: it decides how to say it, and runs on one GPU.** The 32B thinker listens to you, decides when it is its turn, and writes the reply together with inline sound tags: a laugh after a joke, a sigh for bad news, stress on the word that matters. A streaming voice (tag-tts) performs those tags while the reply is still being written. Tags are never read aloud and are removed from the text stream. The whole system is **one vLLM-Omni model**: thinker → tag-tts talker → flow + HiFT vocoder, on a single 80 GB GPU. ## Sophon-Realtime v1 family Three builds share one brain (the same 32B model listens, decides turns and writes the reply). They differ only in how the reply becomes sound. Full comparison: [github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime). | | **Tag** (recommended) | **Flash** | **E2E** | |---|---|---|---| | How it speaks | an expressive speech model performs the sound tags | a lighter, faster speech model speaks the tagged reply | a compact talker (about 350M parameters) generates continuous voice vectors directly, no speech tokens | | NVV-SuperBench (en / zh) | **0.80 / 0.86** | 0.63 / 0.77 | 0.75 / 0.85 | | First audio, one user | ~0.6 s | 0.31 s | **~0.25 s** | | Users per 80 GB GPU (recommended) | 16 | **40** | 16 | | GPUs | 1 | 1 | 1 | | Weights | [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag) | [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) | [Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E) | Pick **Tag** if you want the voice to act; pick **Flash** if users per GPU matter most; pick **E2E** for the fastest first audio with a voice that still laughs and sighs. Tag and Flash share the same APIs; E2E runs on its own engine or, since 1.1.4, on vLLM-Omni with the same APIs as Tag and Flash. ## Highlights - **VoiceBench 82.8 and Big Bench Audio 81.8%: the strongest brain among open full-duplex models.** #1 among open full-duplex models on both; level with GPT-4o-mini-Audio on VoiceBench. - **Paralinguistic understanding 48.6, #1 overall: it hears your tone.** Ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (46.9) and Qwen3-Omni (44.6) on LISTEN, StressTest and MSPB. It hears emotion, emphasis, sarcasm, laughter and sighs straight from your voice. - **The most expressive build: NVV-SuperBench 0.86 (Chinese) and 0.80 (English).** The model decides when to laugh, sigh, breathe, clear its throat or stress a word; the voice performs it instead of reading the tag aloud. - **One 80 GB GPU, one command.** Served by vLLM-Omni; up to 16 concurrent users per GPU, about 0.6 s to first audio. - **Full-Duplex-Bench v3 tool calling: Pass@1 48%, ahead of Grok (43%), with a 100% response rate.** Live mode is compatible with the OpenAI GPT-Live interface. - **Real full duplex.** It listens the whole time you talk and drafts its reply as you go; it picks up when you stop, stops when you cut in, and keeps going when you just say "mm-hm". - **Apache-2.0, free for commercial use.** Fine-tune persona, tone and domain knowledge with ms-swift. Benchmark methods and full comparison tables: [v1 family home page](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-v1). To just try it: [talk to it in the ModelScope Studio](https://www.modelscope.ai/studios/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime). ## Deploy (one GPU, one command) ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime/tag bash install.sh # Python 3.12 venv, vLLM 0.30, vLLM-Omni 0.30, the plugin, and these weights (~42 GB) GPU=0 PORT=8000 bash start.sh # first start 15–20 min (kernels + TensorRT engines), later 5–8 min python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang en --voice ryan_en ``` - APIs: `ws://HOST:8000/v1/realtime` (full duplex: turn-taking, barge-in, backchannel) and `POST /v1/chat/completions` (audio in → text + audio stream). - Voices: `chelsie` (default; `chelsie_zh` / `chelsie_en` picked by language), `vivian_zh`, `ryan_en`, `brand_zh`, `brand_en`. ## Zero-shot voice cloning (new in 1.1) Give it a short clip of any voice and talk to Sophon in that voice. No fine-tuning, no restart. ```bash cp alice.wav model/voices/alice.wav # 3–10 s of clean speech from one speaker (wav or flac, any sample rate) python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang en --voice alice ``` - Use `"voice": "alice"` in `/v1/chat/completions` or in `session.update` on `/v1/realtime`. The clip can be in another language than the reply. - The server prepares new clips in the background within a few seconds, so first audio is as fast as with a built-in voice. Overwrite a file to replace a voice, delete it to remove it. Sound tags (laughs, sighs, …) work with cloned voices too. - 1.1 also updates the voice model (`talker/flow.pt` and its ONNX) so that unseen voices come out much closer to the reference. Needs the latest code: GitHub `main` or `pip install -U "sophon-realtime[trt]"` (1.1.0 or later). - **Only clone your own voice or a voice you have permission to use. Do not use it to impersonate or deceive anyone.** - Hardware: one 80 GB GPU (H100 / H800 / A100 80G), about 65 GB per instance. ## Performance (one H100 80 GB, measured) | Concurrent users (arriving within 10 s) | First audio, median / max | Stutter (median) | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.67 s | ~0 | | 8 | 0.61 / 0.76 s | 0 | | **16** | **0.75 / 1.07 s** | 0.06 s | | 24 | 1.36 / 2.11 s | 0.39 s (queueing starts) | - Full duplex: about 0.7 s from the end of the user's speech to the first voice. - **These numbers need TensorRT.** `install.sh` installs it; with pip, install `pip install "sophon-realtime[trt]"` (CUDA 13). Without TensorRT the voice runs in plain PyTorch and gets about 3× slower under load: at 16 users first audio is about 2.4 s with 1–1.5 s of stutter. Check the server log for `Loaded flow-estimator TensorRT engine`. - **Recommended: up to 16 concurrent users per GPU.** More GPUs: one instance per GPU behind a load balancer; capacity scales roughly linearly. CPU is not a bottleneck (~1.5 cores per instance at 16 users). ## Sound tags `[laughter]`, `[breath]`, `[sigh]`, `[cough]`, `…` (laugh while speaking), `…` (stress a word). Tags are sent to the voice as whole chunks while text streams in, the same way the voice was trained. Event heard when the tag is written (96 test sentences × 2 runs through the full served pipeline, AST detector; 8–12 sentences per class, so ±1 sentence ≈ ±10 points): | | sigh | breath | cough | laugh | |---|---|---|---|---| | this release | 25% | 50% | 33% | 42% | | reference tag-tts renderer, same voice model | 42% | 50% | 33% | 50% | ## Live mode (OpenAI GPT-Live compatible) Run one more command next to the engine and GPT-Live clients can connect by changing only the URL and key. Sophon keeps the voice; when a request needs a lookup or an action it says "Let me check that", hands the task to your backend and speaks the result in its own words. ```bash cd sophon-realtime/live && BUILD=tag PORT=8000 LIVE_PORT=8780 bash start_live.sh # GPT-Live clients: ws://HOST:8780/v1/live/sessions ``` Details and measurements: [live/](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/live/README.md) in the GitHub repository. ## Fine-tuning Fine-tune the thinker's LLM backbone with LoRA in ms-swift to change persona, tone, domain knowledge and tool use. Hearing, the voice and turn-taking stay as released, and sound tags such as laughter and coughs are kept. One 80 GB GPU is enough; see [finetune/](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/finetune/README.md) in the GitHub repository. ## What's inside | folder | what | licence | |---|---|---| | `thinker/` | DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.5 with tag writing merged in, FP8 (with the vision tower) | Apache-2.0 | | `talker/` | tag-tts: language model + distilled flow (4 steps, no CFG) + HiFT; based on Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B | Apache-2.0 | | `voices/` | six reference voices (clip + precomputed prompt) | Apache-2.0 | ## Limitations - `[sigh]` and `…` are still weak; the thinker writes them more often than the voice delivers. - Mandarin is slightly less clear than English with the distilled flow; a laugh is sometimes transcribed as "哈哈" by ASR. - Very long replies (over about a minute of speech in one turn) are beyond what the voice was trained on.

Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E

Sophon-Realtime v1 系列的 E2E 版：单卡、首包约 0.25 秒，声音直接从连续向量里生成
AI降临派（Adventists AI）· Apache-2.0 · v1.3.0

GitHub · Hugging Face · 魔搭 · English

## 这是什么 Sophon-Realtime 是全双工语音对话模型：一个 32B 的大脑负责听你说话、判断你说完没有、写出带声音标签的回复。E2E 版负责把回复变成声音的部分不经过语音 token：一个小巧的说话头（约 3.5 亿参数）在大脑还在写回复时就开始读，边读边生成连续的声音向量（每秒约 6.5 帧），再由 2 步解码器和声码器还原成 24 kHz 音频。笑、咳嗽、叹气、呼吸和重读都由说话头自己在同一条流里发出来。 整套系统（大脑 + 说话头 + 解码器）跑在**一张 80 GB 显卡**上。 ## 1.3.0 更新（2026-11-14） - E2E 版支持零样本音色克隆：给一段 5–12 秒的录音，按名字使用即可，无需微调、无需重启（vLLM-Omni 部署方式，需要代码 1.3.0 及以上）。用法见下面的[音色克隆](#音色克隆)。权重没有变化。 ## 1.2.0 更新（2026-11-13） - 长回复会完整说完，不再限制语音时长（之前约 2 到 2.5 分钟就在句末收住）：说话头把长回复分成约 25–40 秒一段来说，每段都从剩下的文字重新开始。实测在 vLLM-Omni 部署方式下最长说到约 14 分钟。权重没有变化。详见[更新记录](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。 ## 1.1.4 更新（2026-11-12） - E2E 版现在也可以像 Tag、Flash 一样作为一个 vLLM-Omni 模型来部署（代码在 [`e2e/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README_CN.md)），命令、接口（`/v1/realtime`、`/v1/chat/completions`）和客户端都相同。自研引擎的部署方式不变，速度略快。 - 本仓库新增 `thinker/`（已合并回复 LoRA 的大脑，FP8，约 36 GB，与 Tag 仓库里的是同一份文件）、`config.json` 和 `talker220/config.json`，只有 vLLM-Omni 部署方式用到。其他文件没有变化。 - 两种部署方式各自只下载自己需要的部分：自研引擎约 67 GB（不含 `thinker/`），vLLM-Omni 约 41 GB（不含 `base/`、`adapters/`）；安装脚本会自动处理。 ## 1.1.3 更新（2026-11-11） - 与 Tag、Flash 并列为正式版本，从两张卡变成一张卡。 - 新的说话头（`talker220/`），原来的 `talker/` 已移除，下载量少约 8 GB；`base/`、`adapters/`、`e2/`、`voices/` 没有变化。 - 之前的双卡权重保留在本仓库的 `v1.1.0` 标签下（配合代码标签 `v1.1.2` 使用）。 ## 在 v1 系列里的位置 三个版本是同一个大脑（VoiceBench 82.8、Big Bench Audio 81.8%，两项开源全双工第一；副语言理解综合第一），区别只在回复怎么变成声音： | | [Tag](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag)（推荐） | [Flash](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) | **E2E（本仓库）** | |---|---|---|---| | NVV-SuperBench（英 / 中） | **0.80 / 0.86** | 0.63 / 0.77 | 0.75 / 0.85 | | 单路首包 | 约 0.6 秒 | 0.31 秒 | **约 0.25 秒** | | 每张 80 GB 卡建议并发 | 16 路 | **40 路** | 16 路 | | 零样本音色克隆 | 支持 | 支持 | 支持（vLLM-Omni 部署方式） | | 语言 | 中、英和多种欧洲语言 | 同左，另有日、俄 | 中、英 | | 部署 | vLLM-Omni | vLLM-Omni | 自研引擎或 vLLM-Omni | 想要更多语言，用 Tag 或 Flash；想要最快的首包、同时保留会笑会叹气的表现力，用 E2E。 ## 实测（单张 H100 80 GB，全新安装） 语音提问进、语音回答出，全链路都在同一张卡上。首包指从发出请求到收到第一块音频。 | 10 秒内到达的用户数 | 首包 中位数 / P90 | 播放落后超过 0.3 秒的回复数 | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.25 秒 | 0 | | 8 | 0.44 / 0.77 秒 | 0 / 8 | | **16** | **0.44 / 0.56 秒** | **0 / 16** | | 24 | 0.58 / 0.94 秒 | 7 / 24 | | 32 | 0.67 / 0.80 秒 | 23 / 32 | NVV-SuperBench（官方题目与指标，每类每种语言 50 条，Gemini 3 Flash 裁判，F1）： | | 四类合计 | 笑 | 咳嗽 | 叹气 | 呼吸 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 英文 | 0.75 | 0.70 | 0.76 | 0.92 | 0.64 | | 中文 | 0.85 | 0.86 | 0.95 | 0.87 | 0.74 | 同一批句子的转写错字率：中文 3.1%，英文 1.9%。 ## 部署 需要 Linux、NVIDIA 驱动 580 及以上、一张 H100 级的 80 GB 显卡（实际占用约 70 GB）。有两种方式，权重相同、声音相同。 **方式一：自研引擎**（上面表格里的数字） ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime cd sophon-realtime bash scripts/install.sh # 建两个虚拟环境，并从魔搭下载本模型 SOPHON_MODEL_DIR=$PWD/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E GPU=0 bash scripts/start.sh ``` 启动后打开 `http://<服务器>:8000/` 即可在网页里直接对话，也可以通过 WebSocket 接口（`/ws`）接入自己的客户端。详见 [docs/deploy_CN.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/docs/deploy_CN.md)。 **方式二：vLLM-Omni**（与 Tag、Flash 相同的命令和接口） ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime/e2e bash install.sh # 建虚拟环境，并从魔搭下载本模型中需要的部分（约 41 GB） GPU=0 PORT=8000 bash start.sh python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang zh ``` 提供 `ws://<服务器>:8000/v1/realtime`（全双工）和 `/v1/chat/completions`。单张 H100 实测：单路首包约 0.35 秒；16 路首包中位数 0.58–0.65 秒、P90 0.71–0.87 秒，0–2 路回复播放落后超过 0.3 秒；全双工下从说完到出声中位数约 0.45 秒。详见 [e2e/README_CN.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README_CN.md)。 **其他显卡**：以上数字都是在 H100 上测的。在一张 RTX PRO 6000（Blackwell，96 GB）上实测 vLLM-Omni 方式：能安装、能运行，但一张卡只能跟上约 4–8 路并发（E2E 发声部分在这张卡上慢约一倍）。在这类显卡上需要更高并发时，请用 Tag 或 Flash。 ## 音色克隆 需要代码 1.3.0 及以上，vLLM-Omni 部署方式（GitHub 仓库的 `e2e/`）。把录音放进 `model/voices/`，按名字使用： ```bash cp alice.wav model/voices/alice.wav # 5–12 秒、只有一个人说话的清晰录音（wav 或 flac，16 kHz 及以上） python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang zh --voice alice ``` - 需要 Tag 发布包里的两个小模型 `speech_tokenizer_v3.onnx` 和 `campplus.onnx`（约 1 GB），`install.sh` 会自动下载到 `model/clone_frontend/talker/`；本仓库的权重不需要改动。 - 第一次用到时准备并缓存，首包和内置音色一样快；录音太短或读不了时回落内置音色。 - 详细说明见 [e2e/README_CN.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README_CN.md)。 - **请只克隆自己的声音，或已获得声音主人许可的声音；不得用于冒充他人或欺诈。** ## 声音标签 `[laughter]` `[cough]` `[sigh]` `[breath]`（在该位置发出声音）、`词`（重读）、`几个词`（边笑边说）。大脑会自己把它们写进回复；说话头把它们演出来，不会念出来。 ## 这一版的限制 - 一个内置音色；音色克隆只在 vLLM-Omni 部署方式下可用（自研引擎方式暂不支持）。 - 回复用中文或英文。 - 单条回复最长约 4.6 分钟语音（vLLM-Omni 方式约 2.5 分钟）；超出时这条回复在该处正常结束，不影响其他对话。连续说到约 2.5 分钟以内内容是准确的，更长的回复后段会出现念错，建议把单条回复控制在 2.5 分钟以内。 ## 文件 | 目录 | 内容 | |---|---| | `base/` | 大脑的 32B 权重 | | `adapters/tag/` | 写带标签回复的 LoRA | | `talker220/` | 说话头：权重、文字嵌入表、分词器 | | `e2/` | 解码器与声码器 | | `voices/` | 默认音色 | | `thinker/`、`config.json`、`talker220/config.json` | 只有 vLLM-Omni 部署方式用到：已合并回复 LoRA 的大脑（FP8，约 36 GB） | ## 许可证 代码和权重都是 Apache-2.0。第三方组件保留各自的许可证，见 GitHub 仓库的 [NOTICE](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/NOTICE)。 ## 联系 商务合作：jiejin@adventists.ai --- # Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E > **No GPU?** Try it through the hosted API: [sign up](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) and get 3 hours of free voice chat (OpenAI Realtime-compatible, [docs](https://api.adventists.ai/console/docs)). > 🆕 **Smaller GPU?** [Sophon-Realtime-4B-E2E](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-E2E) (v1.4.0) runs this build with a 4B brain on one 32 GB GPU: keeps the turn-taking and sound tags, knows much less. [All builds](https://huggingface.co/collections/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime-6afb357253a3a8905ad758b0) **The E2E build of the Sophon-Realtime v1 family: one GPU, first audio in about 0.25 s, speech generated directly as continuous vectors.** Adventists AI · Apache-2.0 · v1.3.0 ## What it is Sophon-Realtime is a full-duplex voice model: a 32B brain listens to you, decides when you have finished, and writes a reply with sound tags. In the E2E build, the part that turns the reply into sound has no speech-token model in the middle. A compact talker (about 350M parameters) reads the reply while it is still being written and generates a stream of continuous voice vectors, about 6.5 frames per second; a 2-step decoder and a vocoder turn them into 24 kHz audio. Laughs, coughs, sighs, breaths and stressed words are produced by the talker itself, as part of the same stream. The whole system (brain, talker, decoder) runs on **one 80 GB GPU**. ## What's new in 1.3.0 (2026-11-14) - E2E now does zero-shot voice cloning: give it a 5–12 s clip and use the voice by name, with no fine-tuning and no restart (vLLM-Omni deployment, requires code 1.3.0 or later). See [Voice cloning](#voice-cloning) below. The weights are unchanged. ## What's new in 1.2.0 (2026-11-13) - Long replies are spoken to their end, with no limit on speech length (before, speech ended at a sentence end after about 2 to 2.5 minutes): the talker speaks them in segments of about 25–40 s, each a fresh start on the rest of the text. Tested up to about 14 minutes with the vLLM-Omni deployment. The weights are unchanged. See the [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). ## What's new in 1.1.4 (2026-11-12) - E2E can now also be served as one vLLM-Omni model, like Tag and Flash (code in [`e2e/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README.md)), with the same commands, APIs (`/v1/realtime`, `/v1/chat/completions`) and client. The own-engine deployment is unchanged and a little faster. - New in this repository: `thinker/` (the brain with the reply LoRA merged in, FP8, about 36 GB; the same files as in the Tag repository), `config.json` and `talker220/config.json`. Only the vLLM-Omni deployment uses them. Nothing else changed. - Each way of deploying downloads only what it needs: about 67 GB for the own engine (without `thinker/`), about 41 GB for vLLM-Omni (without `base/` and `adapters/`). The install scripts take care of it. ## What's new in 1.1.3 (2026-11-11) - A full build next to Tag and Flash, on one GPU instead of two. - New talker (`talker220/`); the old `talker/` is removed, so the download is about 8 GB smaller. `base/`, `adapters/`, `e2/` and `voices/` are unchanged. - The earlier two-GPU weights stay in this repository at tag `v1.1.0` (use them with code tag `v1.1.2`). ## Where it fits in the v1 family All three builds share one brain (VoiceBench 82.8 and Big Bench Audio 81.8%, #1 among open full-duplex models on both; #1 in paralinguistic understanding). They differ only in how the reply becomes sound: | | [Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag) (recommended) | [Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) | **E2E (this repository)** | |---|---|---|---| | NVV-SuperBench (en / zh) | **0.80 / 0.86** | 0.63 / 0.77 | 0.75 / 0.85 | | First audio, one user | ~0.6 s | 0.31 s | **~0.25 s** | | Recommended users per 80 GB GPU | 16 | **40** | 16 | | Zero-shot voice cloning | yes | yes | yes (vLLM-Omni deployment) | | Languages | Chinese, English and several European languages | the same, plus Japanese and Russian | Chinese, English | | Serving | vLLM-Omni | vLLM-Omni | own engine or vLLM-Omni | Use Tag or Flash for more languages; use E2E for the fastest first audio with a voice that still laughs and sighs. ## Measured (one H100 80 GB, fresh install) Spoken question in, spoken answer out, everything on the same GPU. First audio is the time from sending the request to receiving the first audio chunk. | Users arriving within 10 s | First audio, median / P90 | Replies whose playback fell more than 0.3 s behind | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.25 s | 0 | | 8 | 0.44 / 0.77 s | 0 of 8 | | **16** | **0.44 / 0.56 s** | **0 of 16** | | 24 | 0.58 / 0.94 s | 7 of 24 | | 32 | 0.67 / 0.80 s | 23 of 32 | NVV-SuperBench (official prompts and metric, 50 items per class per language, Gemini 3 Flash judge, F1): | | All 4 | Laugh | Cough | Sigh | Breath | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | English | 0.75 | 0.70 | 0.76 | 0.92 | 0.64 | | Chinese | 0.85 | 0.86 | 0.95 | 0.87 | 0.74 | Transcription error rate on the same sentences: Chinese 3.1%, English 1.9%. ## Deployment Linux, NVIDIA driver 580 or newer, one 80 GB GPU of the H100 class (about 70 GB is used). There are two ways, with the same weights and the same voice. **1. Own engine** (the numbers in the tables above) ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime cd sophon-realtime bash scripts/install.sh # two virtual environments + this model from ModelScope SOPHON_MODEL_DIR=$PWD/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E GPU=0 bash scripts/start.sh ``` Then open `http://:8000/` to talk in the browser, or connect your own client to the WebSocket API (`/ws`). See [docs/deploy.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/docs/deploy.md). **2. vLLM-Omni** (the same commands and APIs as Tag and Flash) ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime/e2e bash install.sh # virtual environment + the parts of this model it needs, from ModelScope (about 41 GB) GPU=0 PORT=8000 bash start.sh python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang en ``` It serves `ws://:8000/v1/realtime` (full duplex) and `/v1/chat/completions`. Measured on one H100: first audio about 0.35 s for one user; 16 users 0.58–0.65 s median / 0.71–0.87 s P90, with 0–2 replies falling more than 0.3 s behind playback; in full duplex about 0.45 s (median) from the end of your speech to the first voice. See [e2e/README.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README.md). **Other GPUs:** all numbers above are measured on an H100. On one RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell, 96 GB) the vLLM-Omni deployment installs and runs, but one GPU keeps up with only about 4–8 concurrent users (the E2E voice stages run about 2× slower on that card). If you need more users per GPU on such cards, use Tag or Flash. ## Voice cloning Requires code 1.3.0 or later and the vLLM-Omni deployment (`e2e/` in the GitHub repository). Put a clip in `model/voices/` and use it by name: ```bash cp alice.wav model/voices/alice.wav # 5-12 s of clean speech from one speaker (wav or flac, 16 kHz or more) python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang en --voice alice ``` - It needs two small models from the Tag release, `speech_tokenizer_v3.onnx` and `campplus.onnx` (about 1 GB); `install.sh` downloads them to `model/clone_frontend/talker/`. The weights in this repository are unchanged. - A voice is prepared the first time it is used and then cached, so first audio is as fast as with the built-in voice; a clip that is too short or cannot be read falls back to the built-in voice. - Details: [e2e/README.md](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/e2e/README.md). - **Only clone your own voice or a voice you have permission to use. Do not use it to impersonate or deceive anyone.** ## Sound tags `[laughter]` `[cough]` `[sigh]` `[breath]` (a sound at that point), `word` (emphasis), `some words` (speaking while laughing). The brain writes them into the reply on its own; the talker performs them instead of reading them aloud. ## Limits of this release - One built-in voice; voice cloning works only with the vLLM-Omni deployment (not yet with the own engine). - Replies are spoken in Chinese or English. - One reply can be at most about 4.6 minutes of speech (about 2.5 minutes with vLLM-Omni); a longer reply ends cleanly at that point and other conversations are not affected. Speech stays accurate up to about 2.5 minutes of continuous talking; beyond that the later part of a reply contains misread words, so keep single replies under 2.5 minutes. ## Files | folder | contents | |---|---| | `base/` | 32B weights of the brain | | `adapters/tag/` | LoRA that writes the tagged reply | | `talker220/` | talker: weights, text embedding table, tokenizer | | `e2/` | decoder and vocoder | | `voices/` | default voice | | `thinker/`, `config.json`, `talker220/config.json` | only for the vLLM-Omni deployment: the brain with the reply LoRA merged in (FP8, about 36 GB) | ## License Code and weights are released under Apache-2.0. Third-party components keep their own licences; see [NOTICE](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/NOTICE) in the GitHub repository. ## Contact Business enquiries: jiejin@adventists.ai

# Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit-MLX

> **No GPU?** Try it through the hosted API: [sign up](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) and get 3 hours of free voice chat (OpenAI Realtime-compatible, [docs](https://api.adventists.ai/console/docs)).


**Version 1.2.0** · [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · code: [`mac/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/tree/main/mac) · CUDA build: [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit) · 中文：`README_CN.md`

The full-duplex speech model [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit), **running locally on an Apple silicon Mac** with MLX.
You talk, it decides by itself when you have finished, answers with its own voice and sound tags, stops when you interrupt, and carries on when you
just say "mm-hmm". Hearing, turn-taking and speaking are all done by the model on the Mac's GPU: no cloud, and no speech-to-text step in between.

The weights are the Flash-4bit weights **repacked losslessly** for MLX: the 4-bit values, scales, audio tower and voice stage are bit-identical to the CUDA build.

## Requirements
- Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 or later
- **36 GB or more unified memory recommended**; 32 GB works with other apps closed (about 26 GB in use while talking)
- About 24 GB download
- A microphone. Mac Studio and Mac mini have none built in: plug in a USB microphone or a headset. Speakers are fine, echo cancellation is built in

## Quick start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime
bash mac/install.sh            # Python environment + this repo's weights, into ~/sophon-mac
~/sophon-mac/sophon            # talk in Chinese
~/sophon-mac/sophon --lang en  # talk in English
```
Options: `--no-aec` (headset, no echo cancellation), `--in` / `--out` (audio devices, `--list` shows them), `--voice`.

## Speed (M4 Max, 36 GB)
| | |
|---|---|
| You stop talking → it starts speaking | **0.9–1.1 s** when the model is sure you have finished; up to about 2.5 s when it waits to see whether you go on |
| Long replies | real time, no stalls |
| You interrupt | it stops within about 0.15 s |
| Model load | about 10 s |

The CUDA server answers in about 0.5 s. On a Mac most of the time goes into the turn decision: when you pause, the model listens to your whole
utterance once on the Mac's GPU. Chips with more GPU cores are faster.

## How turn-taking works on a Mac
To process your audio only once, the turn question is asked inside the reply's own context (system prompt, conversation, your audio, then a short
"has the user finished? A / B" question); if the answer is yes, the reply continues from the same computation. The check schedule and thresholds are
those of the server (0.2 s to 2 s of silence, then a fallback reply). Accuracy on the Smart Turn test set (400 clips per language):

| | English acc. / AUC | Chinese acc. / AUC |
|---|---|---|
| Server turn question | 92.5 / 0.975 | 94.0 / 0.983 |
| **Mac turn question** | **90.5 / 0.960** | **94.3 / 0.977** |

Right after you interrupt, the full four-option question is used instead, so that a short back-channel ("mm-hmm", "yeah") makes it resume the cut reply.

## Echo cancellation
WebRTC AEC3 removes the reply's own sound from the microphone. In a simulated room (speaker sound back at the microphone at −6 dB and 0 dB, 6 s of
reply), the reply never interrupted itself with echo cancellation on (3 / 3 runs) and did every time with it off; a real interruption was still
detected within about 0.12 s.

## Status and limits
- Tested on an M4 Max (36 GB) with real-time simulated audio input (speech played into the engine at real-time pace, simulated room echo).
  Live microphone runs and numbers from other Macs are very welcome in [issue #1](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/issues/1).
- One conversation at a time. Camera input, tool calls and zero-shot voice cloning are not in the Mac version yet (built-in voices only).

## Files
| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| `thinker_mlx/` | the 4-bit thinker for `mlx_lm` (same weights as Flash-4bit) |
| `ear/` | the thinker's audio tower and projector |
| `talker/` | the voice stage (same as Flash) |
| `voices/` | built-in voices |

It listens while you talk, decides from your voice when you have finished, writes a reply with sound tags (`[laughter]` `[cough]` `[sigh]` `[breath]` `…`) and speaks while it writes; a compact talker (about 350M parameters) turns the tagged reply straight into voice vectors; a decoder turns them into sound. # Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash-MLX

> **No GPU?** Try it through the hosted API: [sign up](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) and get 3 hours of free voice chat (OpenAI Realtime-compatible, [docs](https://api.adventists.ai/console/docs)).

**Version 1.5.0** (2026-11-18) · [changelog](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · code: [`mac/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/tree/main/mac) · CUDA build: [Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash) · 32B Mac build: [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit-MLX](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash-4bit-MLX) · 中文：`README_CN.md`

The full-duplex speech model [Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-4B-Flash), **running locally on an Apple silicon Mac with 16 GB or more** (MLX).
You talk, it decides by itself when you have finished, answers with its own voice and sound tags, stops when you interrupt, and carries on when you
just say "mm-hmm". Hearing, turn-taking and speaking are all done by the model on the Mac's GPU: no cloud, and no speech-to-text step in between.

The thinker's language model is quantized to 8 bits by `mlx_lm` (group 64); the audio tower, projector and voice stage are the same weights as the CUDA build.

## 4B or 32B on a Mac

| | **4B (this repo)** | 32B |
|---|---|---|
| Unified memory | **16 GB works** (about 11 GB in use while talking); 24 GB or more recommended | 32 GB works, 36 GB or more recommended (about 26 GB in use) |
| Download | about 9 GB | about 24 GB |
| You stop talking → it starts speaking (M4 Max) | **0.3–0.5 s** when it is sure you have finished | 0.9–1.1 s |
| Knowledge and reasoning | much weaker (VoiceBench 62.4 on the CUDA build) | strong (82.8) |

The 4B brain keeps the conversation skills (turn-taking, back-channels, barge-in, sound tags) but knows and reasons much less, and can state wrong facts with confidence.
It is for local demos, companions and characters; use the 32B build or the [hosted API](https://api.adventists.ai/console/) when answers must be right.

## Requirements
- Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 or later, **16 GB unified memory or more** (with 16 GB, close other apps)
- About 9 GB download
- A microphone. Mac Studio and Mac mini have none built in: plug in a USB microphone or a headset. Speakers are fine, echo cancellation is built in

## Quick start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime
SIZE=4B bash mac/install.sh       # Python environment + this repo's weights, into ~/sophon-mac/models-4b
~/sophon-mac/sophon-4b            # talk in Chinese
~/sophon-mac/sophon-4b --lang en  # talk in English
```
Options: `--no-aec` (headset, no echo cancellation), `--in` / `--out` (audio devices, `--list` shows them), `--voice`. The 32B and 4B builds can be installed side by side.

## Turn-taking
The 4B brain answers the server's four-option turn question ("finished / still talking / back-channel / hesitating"), asked in its own short prompt;
the 32B Mac build's shorter two-option question is tuned for 32B and does not suit 4B (`turn_question` in `config.json` selects it).
Accuracy on a sample of the Smart Turn v3.2 test set (300 clips per language, half of them finished; last 8 s of each):

| | English acc. / AUC | Chinese acc. / AUC |
|---|---|---|
| **4B, this repo** | **90.0 / 0.961** | **89.7 / 0.954** |
| 4B with the 32B build's short question | 72.3 / 0.888 | 74.0 / 0.851 |
| 32B Mac build (same sample) | 91.7 / 0.961 | 92.7 / 0.973 |

When the model is not sure you have finished, it waits up to 2 s of silence before answering.

## Status and limits
- Tested on an M4 Max (36 GB) with real-time simulated audio input, and with MLX memory capped at 10.5 GB (what a 16 GB Mac gives the GPU): the whole
  conversation ran, peak memory 11.3 GB. Not yet tried on a physical 16 GB Mac; reports are very welcome in [issue #1](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/issues/1).
- One conversation at a time. Camera input, tool calls and zero-shot voice cloning are not in the Mac version yet (built-in voices only).

## Files
| Folder | What |
|---|---|
| `thinker_mlx/` | the thinker's language model for `mlx_lm`, 8-bit |
| `ear/` | the thinker's audio tower and projector |
| `talker/` | the voice stage (same as Flash) |
| `voices/` | built-in voices |

Sophon-Realtime v1

中文

**An open full-duplex voice model family that hears your tone and speaks with one.** Adventists AI · Apache-2.0 · **Recommended: [Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag)** · [Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash) · [Try it online](https://huggingface.co/spaces/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime) · [GitHub](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime) Talking to it feels like a phone call with a person: it listens the whole time you talk, picks up as soon as you stop, and stops the moment you cut in. It hears *how* you say things (hesitation, emphasis, sarcasm, laughter, sighs) and answers with tone of its own: it laughs, sighs and clears its throat when the conversation calls for it. This is the home page of the Sophon-Realtime v1 family. **Three builds share one brain** (the same 32B model listens, decides when to take the turn and writes the reply); they differ only in how the reply becomes sound. **Start with Tag: this repository holds the 32B-Tag weights** (byte-identical to [Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag)), so you can download and serve the recommended build straight from here.

## Three builds: which one? | | **[Tag](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag) (recommended)** | **[Flash](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash)** | **[E2E](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E)** | |---|---|---|---| | How it speaks | the brain writes the reply with sound tags; an expressive speech model performs them | the same tagged reply, spoken by a lighter, faster speech model | a compact talker (about 350M parameters) generates continuous voice vectors directly, no speech tokens | | Best for | expressive voice: companions, characters, demos | speed and scale: customer service, in-car, many users per GPU | expressive voice with the fastest first audio | | Non-verbal sounds (NVV-SuperBench, zh / en) | **0.86 / 0.80** | 0.77 / 0.63 | 0.85 / 0.75 | | First audio, one user | ~0.6 s | 0.31 s | **~0.25 s** | | Users per 80 GB GPU (recommended) | 16 | **40** | 16 | | GPUs | **1** | **1** | **1** | | Serving | vLLM-Omni, one command | vLLM-Omni, one command | own engine or vLLM-Omni, one command | Pick **Tag** if you want the voice to act; pick **Flash** if users per GPU matter most; pick **E2E** for the fastest first audio with a voice that still laughs and sighs. Tag and Flash share the same APIs, so you can switch later; E2E runs on its own engine or, since 1.1.4, on vLLM-Omni with the same APIs as Tag and Flash. ## Highlights - **VoiceBench 82.8 and Big Bench Audio 81.8%: the strongest brain among open full-duplex models.** #1 among open full-duplex models on both; level with GPT-4o-mini-Audio on VoiceBench. All three builds share this brain. - **Paralinguistic understanding 48.6, #1 overall: it hears your tone.** Ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (46.9) and Qwen3-Omni (44.6) on LISTEN, StressTest and MSPB. Its ears are DuplexJev, our open speech-decision model. - **NVV-SuperBench 0.86 (Chinese) and 0.80 (English) with the Tag build: it speaks with tone.** The model decides when to laugh, sigh, breathe or clear its throat, and the voice performs it instead of reading the tag aloud. - **Fast: first audio in about 0.25 s with E2E and 0.31 s with Flash.** It drafts its reply while you talk; when you cut in, it stops and answers your new question. - **Full-Duplex-Bench v3 tool calling: Pass@1 48%, ahead of Grok (43%), with a 100% response rate: it gets work done.** [Live mode](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/live/README.md) is compatible with the OpenAI GPT-Live interface and lets it work with a larger backend model. Every reply comes with an auditable transcript. - **One 80 GB GPU for every build, one command.** Tag and Flash are served by vLLM-Omni; up to 16 (Tag, E2E) or 40 (Flash) concurrent users per GPU. Apache-2.0 code and weights, free for commercial use. ## Quick start (Tag) Quickest: ```bash pip install "sophon-realtime[trt]" # Python 3.12, Linux, CUDA 13; keep [trt]: without TensorRT the voice is ~3x slower under load sophon-realtime serve # downloads the Tag weights (~42 GB) on first run, then serves on port 8000 ``` Or download the weights from this repository: ```bash hf download adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-v1 --local-dir Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag # ~45 GB: thinker/, talker/, voices/, config.json ``` Or use the one-command scripts (isolated environment): ```bash git clone https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime && cd sophon-realtime/tag bash install.sh # venv + vLLM-Omni + plugin, and downloads the Tag weights (~42 GB) GPU=0 PORT=8000 bash start.sh # first start 15–20 min, later 5–8 min python client_example.py --wav my_question.wav --lang en --voice ryan_en ``` - APIs: `ws://HOST:8000/v1/realtime` (full duplex: turn-taking, barge-in, back-channels) and `POST /v1/chat/completions` (audio in, text + audio out). - Flash works the same way; see the [Flash page](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash). To just try it, talk to it on [Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime). ## Live mode: a drop-in for OpenAI GPT-Live [`live/`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/sophon-realtime/blob/main/live/README.md) in the GitHub repository is a gateway that speaks the OpenAI GPT-Live protocol in front of a Tag or Flash engine: GPT-Live clients switch by changing the URL and key. Sophon keeps the voice; when a request needs a lookup or an action it says a short "Let me check that", hands the task to your backend and speaks the result in its own words. A larger model can also run the back office: with DeepSeek V4 Pro, Big Bench Audio rises from 81.2 to about 83. To start it, run one more command next to a Tag or Flash engine started with the one-command scripts: ```bash cd sophon-realtime/live && BUILD=tag PORT=8000 LIVE_PORT=8780 bash start_live.sh # GPT-Live clients: ws://HOST:8780/v1/live/sessions ``` ## Benchmark details ### Conversation: VoiceBench (official evaluators, gpt-4o-mini judge) | model | full-duplex | open weights | overall | |---|:-:|:-:|:-:| | GPT-4o-Audio | — | — | 86.8 | | **Sophon-Realtime v1** | ✅ | ✅ | **82.8** | | GPT-4o-mini-Audio | — | — | 82.8 | | MiniCPM-o 4.5 | ✅ | ✅ | 76.1 | | MiniCPM-o 2.6 | ✅ | ✅ | 71.2 | | Freeze-Omni | ✅ | ✅ | 55.2 | | NemotronLabs VoiceChat | ✅ | ✅ | 55.1 | | PersonaPlex | ✅ | ✅ | 30.6 | | Moshi | ✅ | ✅ | 29.5 | AlpacaEval uses the 199-question standard subset. Other scores come from the VoiceBench leaderboard and from Table 3 of the NemotronLabs VoiceChat paper (arXiv:2609.21967); the MiniCPM-o 4.5 score there is from an independent evaluation. ### Spoken reasoning: Big Bench Audio 1,000 spoken reasoning questions, graded on what the model actually says. | model | open weights | accuracy | |---|:-:|:-:| | GPT-Live-1 | — | 90% | | **Sophon-Realtime v1** | ✅ | **81.8%** | | Raon SpeechChat | ✅ | 58% | | Freeze-Omni | ✅ | 33% | | PersonaPlex | ✅ | 19% | | Moshi | ✅ | 4% | Sophon: self-run, with spoken answers transcribed and judged by gpt-4.1. Others: Artificial Analysis leaderboard. ### Tool calling: Full-Duplex-Bench v3 Disfluent real human speech with multi-step tool calls. 100 tasks, judged by GPT-4o. | model | open weights | Pass@1 ↑ | responds when it should ↑ | |---|:-:|:-:|:-:| | GPT-Realtime | — | 60% | 96% | | Gemini Live 3.1 | — | 54% | — | | **Sophon-Realtime** | ✅ | **48%** | **100%** | | cascaded pipeline | — | 45% | — | | Grok | — | 43% | — | | Ultravox v0.7 | ✅ | 41% | — | Sophon: best of several runs. Others: official Full-Duplex-Bench v3 results. ### Hearing tone: paralinguistic understanding Sophon-Realtime listens with [DuplexJev](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/AdventistsAI/DuplexJev-32B-Para). These benchmarks test emotion, sarcasm, stress and intonation. | model | LISTEN (4 tasks) + StressTest + MSPB, combined | |---|:-:| | **DuplexJev (Sophon-Realtime's ears)** | **48.6** | | Gemini 3.8 Flash | 46.9 | | Qwen3-Omni | 44.6 | ### Speaking with tone: NVV-SuperBench Checks whether the laughs, coughs, sighs and breaths a reply calls for actually show up in the audio. Official scripts, 50 items per category, judged by Gemini 3 Flash; higher F1 is better. | model | Chinese | English | |---|:-:|:-:| | Sophon-Realtime-32B-Tag | **0.86** | **0.80** | | Sophon-Realtime-32B-Flash | 0.77 | 0.63 | | Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E | 0.85 | 0.75 | All three builds speak the same tagged reply texts; only the voice differs. ## How it works - **Listens continuously.** At each pause, the same model decides in a single token whether you've finished, are still talking, are back-channeling or are thinking. - **Drafts early, speaks on time.** A reply is drafted from your first pause and released the moment the model decides it's its turn. If you keep talking, the draft is dropped before you hear it. - **Writes how to say it, not just what.** The brain marks where to laugh, sigh, breathe, cough or stress a word; All three builds perform these marks and never read them aloud. - **Text half a step ahead, voice in step.** Text and voice stream together, so every reply has a transcript for audits, tools and larger backend models. - **Remembers what you actually heard.** History keeps the real audio of both sides. When you interrupt, only the part you heard is kept. - **E2E: speech as continuous vectors.** In the E2E build a compact talker (about 350M parameters) reads the tagged reply while it is still being written and generates continuous voice vectors directly, with no speech tokens in between; a 2-step decoder turns them into sound. First audio comes in about 0.25 s on one GPU. See the [E2E page](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/Sophon-Realtime-32B-E2E). ## Fine-tuning Fine-tune the thinker's LLM backbone with LoRA in ms-swift to change persona, tone, domain knowledge and tool use. The audio encoder and the voice stay as released, and turn-taking is not affected. Training continues the bundled tag LoRA (`adapters/tag`), so laughter, coughs and other sound tags are kept. ## Quick Start

### A. Full `Q4_K` / `Q5_K` on Official `speech.cpp` (`v0.11.2+`, Vulkan / CPU)

Keep the matching `.gguf.json` sidecar beside the `.gguf` file (`max_text_tokens: 8192`, `voice_codec: 2cf2ec268a087bd2ad91bfbb6796b0429fb03a73cdb8fd07f445d503e9a14d37`). On Vulkan, export the three `GGML_VK_DISABLE_*` flags:

```bash
export GGML_VK_DISABLE_F16=1
export GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1
export GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT2=1

# 1. Extract a reusable voice prompt
./build/speech voice Drama-35B-A3B-Japanese-v3-Q4_K.gguf ref.wav \
  --transcript "参照音声の正確な書き起こし" \
  speaker.voice.gguf

# 2. Synthesize Japanese speech on Vulkan
./build/speech tts Drama-35B-A3B-Japanese-v3-Q4_K.gguf \
  --device Vulkan0 \
  --voice speaker.voice.gguf \
  --seed 42 \
  -o out.wav \
  "深夜の図書館は静かで、ページをめくる音だけが規則正しく響いていた。"

# 3. Optional local server
./build/speech serve Drama-35B-A3B-Japanese-v3-Q4_K.gguf \
  --device Vulkan0 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8080
```

### B. 12–24 GB CUDA GPUs (`Drama-35B-A3B-Japanese-v3-small-IQ3_XXS.gguf` + Fast CUDA Patch)

`drama3-speechcpp-fast.patch` targets `speech.cpp v0.11.2` and delivers ~`2.96×` aggregate CUDA speedup (`drama3-small-speechcpp.patch` provides the minimal `IQ3_XXS` compatibility patch without the CUDA speed optimizations):

```bash
  -o small_out.wav \

```

## Important Backend & VRAM Notes

- **Use Vulkan or CPU for Full `Q4_K` / `Q5_K` (Do Not Use CUDA):** Upstream `ggml-cuda` stores `block_q8_1.ds` in FP16, which overflows on `ffn_down_exps` activations and triggers `not finite numbers` assertions on CUDA. Run Full `Q4_K` / `Q5_K` on Vulkan (with all three `GGML_VK_DISABLE_*=1` flags) or CPU (`block_q8_K`), and use `Drama-35B-A3B-Japanese-v3-small-IQ3_XXS.gguf` for CUDA GPUs.
- **VRAM Placement Overhead (`placement.cpp`):** `speech.cpp` adds `~2.40 GiB` of compute/KV reserve (`kComputeBytes = 1536 MiB` + runtime overhead) to weight bytes (`~23.21 GiB` for `Q4_K`, `~26.96 GiB` for `Q5_K`, `~11.48 GiB` for `small-IQ3_XXS`). On desktop 24 GB Windows GPUs with ~19–21 GiB free VRAM, `Q4_K` spills ~6–10 expert layers (`~0.42 GiB`/layer) to CPU rather than fitting all layers on GPU.
- **Voice Cloning & Stage/Emotion Tags:** Reference cloning (`--voice speaker.voice.gguf`) produces noticeably cleaner, more consistent prosody than text-only voice design, especially on whispered or multi-clause prompts. Inline emotion and stage tags follow [TAG_LIST.md](https://huggingface.co/Aratako/Drama-3-Japanese/blob/main/TAG_LIST.md).

### Stratified Japanese `imatrix` Calibration

- Calibrated in **BF16** across **300 stratified Japanese sequences** drawn from JSUT and JVNV (`10,240` expert layers/groups; `840` low-hit entries `<8` shrunk toward layer mean; `391` zero-hit entries smoothed).
- Captured extreme activation dynamic range in `ffn_down_exps` (channel-wise `mean(x²)` up to `6.77×10⁸`), protecting MoE routing and sensitive non-expert tensors during quantization.

- **Routed Experts (`Q4_K` `18.12 GB` `file_type=14` / `Q5_K` `22.15 GB` `file_type=16`):** Routed MoE expert FFN projections.

- **`F16` (`781.8 MB`):** Audio codec convolutions and matrices.
- **`F32` (`107.1 MB`):** Layer norms, MoE routers, `ffn_gate_inp_shexp`, SSM state/gate parameters (`ssm_in_a`, `ssm_in_b`, `ssm_conv1d`, `ssm_dt_bias`, `ssm_a_log`, `ssm_norm`), codec codebooks, and biases.

# Pocket TTS Voice Cloning for LiteRT

This repository contains **22 Pocket TTS model packs covering 26 languages**, exported to LiteRT for on-device speech synthesis. Each pack can synthesize speech in a voice conditioned on a short reference WAV. The output is mono audio at **24 kHz**.

The graphs store weights in **FP16** and use **FP32** inputs and outputs. The export notebook checks each graph on LiteRT CPU. Performance depends on the device and checkpoint. The Korean and Welsh packs use larger 24-layer models.

## Languages

| Checkpoints | Languages |
| --- | --- |
| Official Kyutai | English, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish |
| Community language packs | Czech, Estonian, Greek, Gujarati, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Mandarin Chinese, Persian, Polish, Turkish, Welsh, Wolof |
| Shared Indic multilingual pack | English, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu |

The January English checkpoint and the newer English checkpoint are available as separate packs. The six Indic language options share one download.

## Choose a pack

Open `pocket-tts-index.json` to find the pack for your target language. Download the files listed in that pack's `pocket-tts.json`. The manifest also records tensor shapes, text preprocessing rules, source checkpoint information, and SHA-256 checksums.

Each pack includes four `.tflite` graphs for reference-audio encoding, autoregressive generation, and the two Mimi decoding stages. It also includes the tokenizer and the weights used by the host code. The host tokenizes the text, maintains the generation cache, and assembles the audio. The accompanying Colab notebook shows how to run the complete pipeline with a reference WAV.

## Credits and licenses

Pocket TTS and the Mimi codec were developed by [Kyutai](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts). The conversion builds on [john-rocky’s LiteRT exporter](https://github.com/john-rocky/LiteRT-Models/tree/main/pockettts). See the `README.md` inside each pack for its original checkpoint, authors, and license. Use reference recordings with the speaker’s permission.

# Sakhiya-Pro v1 — Nepal-native anchor teacher TTS (OmniVoice-600M fine-tune)

Large GPU teacher voice for the Sakhiya project (NEBians News voiceovers; later a teacher for tiny browser models).
Full-backbone bf16 fine-tune of `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` (Qwen3-0.6B + 8-codebook audio tokens, `language="npi"`) on a single
Nepal-native female anchor (OpenSLR SLR43 speaker 6834 + Seed-VC-unified SLR43/Vedic/news clips).

## Use
```bash
pip install omnivoice  # + soundfile jiwer librosa
python sakhiya_pro_render.py --model . --text "नमस्ते, म सखिया।" --out hello.wav   # Best-of-3 + broadcast chain (-14 LUFS)
```
`anchor_ref.wav` / `anchor_ref.json` is the reference prompt (the anchor timbre). Always pass it as `ref_audio` / `ref_text`.

## Honest evaluation (synthesized audio, 8 hard sentences; automatic metrics only — no human MOS)
See `EVAL.md` in this repo for the table (base zero-shot vs fine-tune checkpoints). Metrics: Kriti Nepali CTC-ASR CER, UTMOS22,
ECAPA similarity to the anchor, Hindi-leak count, click forensics.

## Known limits
* Fine-tune data is ~1.9 h, mostly read speech (SLR43); news-style prosody comes from the base model, not from new news data.
* The base model has higher UTMOS / lower Vedic CER than the fine-tune; the fine-tune buys speaker lock (ECAPA sim 0.55 → 0.745) at equal UTMOS (~4.0) — selected checkpoint `ft3_s200` (light 200-step, LR 3e-6 adaptation).
* ai4bharat/IndicF5 was gated (403); Swar (F5-Base fine-tune) represented the F5 family in the bake-off.
* No human listening test was run by the assistant; please listen to `samples/` before broadcast use.

# LvW-Ming-TTS-0.5B MLX (4bit)

[Lucasgitguy-co/LvW-Ming-TTS-0.5B](https://huggingface.co/Lucasgitguy-co/LvW-Ming-TTS-0.5B) converted for
[mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) with `mlx_audio.convert` (mlx-audio 0.6.6), 4-bit affine quantization.
`campplus.safetensors` is the speaker encoder converted with mlx-audio's own converter.

> **Release gate: FAILED.** This fine-tune is not better than the base model on the held-out test.
> It is published as-is so the result can be inspected; for real use, the base model is the safer choice.
>
> | Rule (set before training) | Base | This model | Result |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Mean error lower than base | 6.99% | 7.11% | **FAIL** |
> | Stop failures not higher | 2/420 | 3/420 | **FAIL** |
> | No language more than 10% (+0.5 pt) worse | | es worse | **FAIL** |

Format check **FAILED** (rule: mean error at most 10% + 0.5 pt above the PyTorch model on the same sentences): 30 held-out en/zh sentences, mean error 9.38% vs
6.91% for the PyTorch model (same sentences and voices).

```bash
pip install -U "mlx-audio>=0.6.1"
mlx_audio.tts.generate --model Lucasgitguy-co/LvW-Ming-TTS-0.5B-MLX-4bit --voice US_Emma \
  --text "The evening wind blew in from the mountain pass."
# voice cloning: --ref_audio reference.wav --ref_text "Exact transcript of reference.wav."
# other languages: --lang_code de|es|fr|ko|ja
```

mlx-audio 0.6.0 and earlier load the model but say the wrong words; use 0.6.1 or later.
mlx-audio limits that apply: CAM++ speaker embeddings are not extracted automatically, and text
normalization is not ported (write numbers as words).

## Responsible use

Inherited from the base model: voice cloning and built-in voices are for research and
legitimate creative use. Do not impersonate a real person without consent, deceive, or break
the law. Label synthetic speech as synthetic where it could be mistaken for a real recording.
